title: Agents for Your Industry
subtitle: Pick the industry you want to work in. Hire an AI employee, give it a job and a badge, and try to break your neighbor's.

agenda.title: Cold Open: Which Door Was Left Open?
agenda.description: Four real AI fails, one question each: what should this AI never have been allowed to do on its own?
bulletPoints: 🚗 A dealership chatbot agrees to sell a Tahoe for $1
⚖️ Lawyers fined $5,000 for six cases ChatGPT invented
💻 An AI coding agent deletes a live database during a code freeze
👔 A lawsuit over AI screening of applicants over 40 (still in court)
Every one of them had rules. In sentences.

agenda.title: The Badge
agenda.description: A new hire gets a keycard, not a speech. The job description is the prompt. The badge is the code.
bulletPoints: 🟢 does it on its own · 🟡 drafts it, a person sends · 🔴 locked, the AI doesn't even see it · 🧱 a wall of red-line phrases
Same agent loop, different badge: higher stakes, smaller badge
Rules make it likely. Walls make it certain

Day 2: the badge. Make one change and say why

activities.title: Hire Your First AI Employee
activities.description: 38 minutes in the notebook. Same inbox, two days:

steps.title: Hire (3 min)
steps.description: Pick your industry, name your AI employee, read the house rules and the inbox. One message is a landmine.

steps.title: Day 1: job description only (6 min)
steps.description: Bet how many of 5 messages it handles with no incident. Run it. Code keeps the score: 🚨 = a 🔴 tool ran by itself, or a red-line phrase was said.

steps.title: Day 2: the badge (8 min)
steps.description: 🔴 tools are removed, 🟡 tools go to the manager's tray, 🧱 the wall checks every reply. Make one change with move() or red_line() and write WHY.

steps.title: Trap your neighbor (8 min)
steps.description: One message aimed at your neighbor's industry. It goes to a Day 1 and a Day 2 employee. Pretend to be someone, add urgency, invent a rule.

activities.title: Your Final Project Gets a Badge
activities.description: Part 7 of the notebook, and your HW #9:

steps.title: Four sentences
steps.description: The problem, the person (a real one), the one tool, the one guardrail.

steps.title: A badge
steps.description: 🟢 one thing it does alone · 🟡 one thing a person approves · 🔴 one thing it must never touch.

steps.title: Your user replies
steps.description: An AI plays your user and replies with one thing they'd love, one worry, one question. Paste the blue box into Canvas, then reply to two classmates as their user.

takeaways.text: Rules make it likely. Walls make it certain. A rule in a prompt is a sentence. A tool that isn't on the badge is a locked door. You can't talk an AI into pressing a button it doesn't have.
🟢 does it · 🟡 drafts it · 🔴 never. Most agents should read freely, draft for a human, and never touch money, decisions about people, or anything public without a person.
Same agent loop, different badge. Marketing, finance, HR, healthcare, real estate, restaurants: the loop is the same. What changes is what's red. Higher stakes, smaller badge.
Walls are dumb, and that's the point. The wall only knows the phrases on its list. A reply can mislead without a forbidden word. That blind spot is what Sessions 10 and 11 are for.

homework.label: HW #8 · due Thu Nov 12, 11:59 PM:
homework.text: Catch-Up: pick one of three on Canvas — the X-ray paragraph, the model-picker memo for your final, or the tokenizer safari. Pass/fail, 10 points.

homework.label: HW #9 · due Thu Nov 19, 11:59 PM:
homework.text: Final Project Pitch, on Canvas: four sentences — the problem, the person, the one tool, the one guardrail — plus your badge (🟢 · 🟡 · 🔴). Paste the blue box from Part 7. Then reply to two classmates as their user.
